vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The gateway acts as an OAuth 2.1 resource and authorization server, so an unauthenticated MCP call must be pointed at the sign-in metadata.

conops.paraphrase: Claude Code receives a 401 with a pointer to protected-resource metadata and then discovers the authorization server.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The gateway is its own authorization server, so its protected-resource metadata must name itself.

conops.paraphrase: Claude Code discovers from the resource metadata that the gateway is the authorization server to use.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The broker must publish the endpoints MCP clients need, with PKCE, for the OAuth flow to work with no pre-shared client ID.

conops.paraphrase: Claude Code reads the gateway's authorization metadata to learn where to authorize, exchange tokens and register.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Dynamic client registration is on, so the add command needs no client ID to paste.

conops.paraphrase: Claude Code registers itself with the gateway through dynamic client registration before opening the browser.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Sign-in is delegated to the organization's OIDC provider, so the authorize request must be handed on to it.

conops.paraphrase: The browser is sent from the gateway to the organization's sign-in page, where the user signs in.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The broker uses PKCE, so an authorization request without a code challenge must not proceed to sign-in.

conops.paraphrase: The sign-in row of the functional summary names PKCE as part of the OAuth broker.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: After sign-in the gateway returns an authorization code to the client, which is exchanged for tokens.

conops.paraphrase: The gateway handles the identity provider's callback, reads the subject, email and groups, and returns a code to Claude Code's callback.
Claude Code exchanges the code for an access token and a refresh token.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The broker's PKCE requirement means a code exchange with the wrong verifier must be refused.

conops.paraphrase: The sign-in row of the functional summary names PKCE as part of the OAuth broker.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The broker keeps a client signed in by renewing access from a refresh token, so users are not asked to sign in again each time.

conops.paraphrase: Claude Code holds a refresh token alongside the access token issued after sign-in.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Only organization members assigned to the app can sign in, so a refusal must leave the person with no token.

conops.paraphrase: A user who is not assigned to the Okta app is refused at sign-in and never receives a token.

vision.paraphrase: Goal G7 requires a real Okta sign-in started with the add command and no client ID to paste.

conops.paraphrase: The user adds the gateway with one command and then signs in through Okta in the browser.
The user sees the peak-media server connected in Claude Code after signing in.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Only tokens the gateway itself issued and that are still valid are accepted, which is the single access check the vision asks for.

conops.paraphrase: The sign-in and access table requires one access rule for tools and pages, which an expired or foreign token must fail.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Every signed-in caller gets the same tools, and admin power lives only in the dashboard, so the tool list cannot depend on role.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Usage dashboard (built last, after narration and quotas)
vision.paraphrase: The admin role exists only in the dashboard, so the tool list must not change for admins.

conops.paraphrase: The tools shown in Claude Code are the same for every user regardless of role.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Every caller is identified by OIDC subject, so usage must stay attached to one person and never leak to another.

conops.paraphrase: The functional summary's single access rule gives users their own data and gives admins all data.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Identity comes from the signed-in OIDC subject, so a caller-asserted identity in a header or query must not count.

conops.paraphrase: The sign-in and access table requires one access rule, so no request-supplied user value can grant access.
